name: Matrix operations
text:
Compute the scalar multiple $$ -3\left[ \begin{array}{rrr} 3 \amp 1 \amp 0 \\ -4 \amp 3 \amp -1 \\ \end{array} \right] $$ .

Find the sum $$ \left[ \begin{array}{rr} 0 \amp -3 \\ 1 \amp -2 \\ 3 \amp 4 \\ \end{array} \right] + \left[ \begin{array}{rrr} 4 \amp -1 \\ -2 \amp 2 \\ 1 \amp 1 \\ \end{array} \right] $$ .

$\left[\begin{array}{rr} 4 \amp -4 \\ -1 \amp 0 \\ 4 \amp 5 \\ \end{array}\right] $

Suppose that $A$ and $B$ are two matrices. What do we need to know about their shapes before we can form the sum $A+B$?

The shapes must be the same.

The shapes must be the same.

The matrix $I_n$, which we call the identity matrix, is the $n\times n$ matrix whose entries are zero except for the diagonal entries, all of which are 1. For instance, $$ I_3 = \left[ \begin{array}{rrr} 1 \amp 0 \amp 0 \\ 0 \amp 1 \amp 0 \\ 0 \amp 0 \amp 1 \\ \end{array} \right] $$ . If we can form the sum $A+I_n$, what must be true about the matrix $A$?

The shape of $A$ must be $n\times n$.

The shape of $A$ must be $n\times n$.

Find the matrix $ A - 2I_3$ where $$ A = \left[ \begin{array}{rrr} 1 \amp 2 \amp -2 \\ 2 \amp -3 \amp 3 \\ -2 \amp 3 \amp 4 \\ \end{array} \right] $$ .

$ A-2I_3 = \left[\begin{array}{rrr} -1 \amp 2 \amp -2 \\ 2 \amp -5 \amp 3 \\ -2 \amp 3 \amp 2 \\ \end{array}\right] $

$ A-2I_3 = \left[\begin{array}{rrr} -1 \amp 2 \amp -2 \\ 2 \amp -5 \amp 3 \\ -2 \amp 3 \amp 2 \\ \end{array}\right] $
